svg.title: Read every page, or follow three pointers
svg.desc: On the left, a sequential scan drawn as seventy-two heap pages all swept, removing 333,332 rows per worker in 86.8 milliseconds. On the right, a B-tree with the descent path from root through one internal node to one leaf traced in bold with numbered steps, reaching the row in 0.033 milliseconds, with 1970x written between them. Below, a composite index on (customer_id, placed_at) is drawn as sorted keys grouped by customer, serving a leftmost-prefix query in 0.512 ms while a second-column-only predicate falls back to a 116.6 ms scan.
svg.text: Read every page, or follow three pointers
Rows Removed by Filter: 333 332 per worker
WHERE customer_id = 900 ORDER BY placed_at -> 0.512 ms
sorted by the FIRST column first. The second is
only ordered WITHIN one value of the first.
the indexes are bigger than the table
50 000 inserts: 788.9 ms with no indexes, 1 591.8 ms with five
...and when IS the seq scan faster?
